definition_en: the number 11, the hour on a clock, or a team of eleven players
core_image: 钟面上的短针指向十一，旁边站着十一个孩子

sceneCN: 这里 eleven 是「十一」（第 01 个义项）；句意是房间里有十一个孩子。

senses.title: The number 11
senses.definition: the number 11
senses.example: There are eleven children in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里有十一个孩子。
senses.why: Old English endleofan is literally 'one left', meaning one beyond ten; that is why the word counts the first number after ten.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 endleofan 字面是「剩下一个」，即过了十还多一个；这个词因此表示十之后的第一个数。

senses.title: Eleven o'clock
senses.definition: eleven o'clock
senses.example: We have lunch at eleven.
senses.exampleCN: 我们十一点吃午饭。
senses.why: Clock faces use the same counting words for hours, so the number eleven also names the hour before noon.
senses.whyCN: 钟面用同一套计数词报时，所以十一也指中午之前的那一个小时。

senses.title: A team of eleven players
senses.definition: a team of eleven players
senses.example: The school eleven won the match.
senses.exampleCN: 校队赢了比赛。
senses.why: Football and cricket put exactly eleven players on the field, so the number itself became a name for the side.
senses.whyCN: 足球和板球场上正好十一个人，这个数字本身就成了球队的称呼。

definition_en: other than the thing mentioned, or if not
core_image: 桌上只剩一只空杯子，孩子探头问还有没有别的东西
scene: 桌上只剩一只空杯子，孩子问还有没有别的东西。Is there anything else in the box?
sceneCN: 这里 else 是「别的（事物）」（第 01 个义项）；句意是盒子里还有别的东西吗？

senses.title: Other things
senses.definition: other things besides what is mentioned
senses.example: Is there anything else in the box?
senses.exampleCN: 盒子里还有别的东西吗？
senses.why: Old English elles meant 'otherwise, in another way'; used after words like anything, it came to mean other things.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 elles 意为「否则、以另一种方式」；用在 anything 一类词后，就表示其他事物。

senses.title: A different person
senses.definition: a different person
senses.example: Someone else took my seat.
senses.exampleCN: 别人坐了我的位子。
senses.why: The same 'other than the one named' idea is applied to people after someone, everyone and nobody.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「不是所指的那个」的意思，用在 someone、everyone、nobody 之后便指另一个人。

senses.title: If not
senses.definition: if not; otherwise
senses.example: Hurry up, or else we will miss the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们赶不上公交车。
senses.why: The oldest sense 'in another way' survives in or else, which names the different outcome if nothing is done.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思「以另一种方式」保留在 or else 里，表示什么都不做时的另一种结果。

definition_en: a message sent by computer, or to send such a message
core_image: 屏幕上亮起一封新邮件，收件箱的未读数字跳了一下
scene: 屏幕上亮起一封新邮件，收件箱的未读数字跳了一下。A new email appears on the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 email 是「电子邮件」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她今天早上给我发了一封电子邮件。

senses.title: An electronic message
senses.definition: a message sent electronically
senses.example: She sent me an email this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她今天早上给我发了一封电子邮件。
senses.why: The prefix e- stands for electronic, so email is literally an electronic piece of mail, named after the paper mail it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 e- 是 electronic 的缩写，email 字面就是「电子信件」，沿用了它所取代的纸质邮件的说法。

senses.title: The email service
senses.definition: the service used to send such messages
senses.example: Please contact me by email.
senses.exampleCN: 请通过电子邮件联系我。
senses.why: Once the message had a name, the same word named the channel, just as 'by mail' names a way of sending.
senses.whyCN: 这种信件有了名字之后，同一个词也指传递它的渠道，正如 by mail 指一种寄送方式。

senses.title: To send by email
senses.definition: to send a message electronically
senses.example: I will email you the photos.
senses.exampleCN: 我会把照片发电子邮件给你。
senses.why: English turns communication nouns into verbs (mail, text, phone), and email followed that pattern.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把通信类名词用作动词，如 mail、text、phone，email 也沿用了这一模式。

definition_en: to get pleasure from something, or to have the use of something good
core_image: 孩子捧着故事书坐在窗边，读到有趣处笑出声
scene: 孩子捧着故事书坐在窗边，读到有趣处笑出声。The children enjoy the story very much.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoy 是「享受」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们非常享受这个故事。

pos.zh: 动词：享受、享有、过得愉快

senses.title: To take pleasure in
senses.definition: to get pleasure from something
senses.example: The children enjoy the story very much.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们非常享受这个故事。
senses.why: From Old French enjoier, 'give joy', built on Latin gaudere 'rejoice'; the English verb keeps the plain idea of having joy in something.
senses.whyCN: 源自古法语 enjoier「给予快乐」，其根是拉丁语 gaudere「欢欣」；英语这个词保留的就是「从某事中得到快乐」的意思。

senses.title: To have good health
senses.definition: to have the use of something good
senses.definitionCN: 拥有并受益于好的事物
senses.example: She enjoys good health at eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 她八十岁仍享有健康。
senses.why: The 'have joy in' sense widened to 'have the use of' a good thing, as when someone possesses health or rights.
senses.whyCN: 「从中得乐」的意思扩大为「拥有并使用」某种好的事物，如拥有健康或权利。

senses.title: To have a good time
senses.definition: to have a good time
senses.example: We enjoyed ourselves at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在聚会上玩得很愉快。
senses.why: In enjoy oneself the joy moves from the thing to the person's own experience, so the phrase means to have a good time.
senses.whyCN: 在 enjoy oneself 中，快乐从事物转到人自身的经历，这个短语因此表示玩得开心。

definition_en: a small rubber or pad used to remove pencil or chalk marks
core_image: 铅笔字写歪了，孩子从笔袋里摸出一块小橡皮
scene: 铅笔字写歪了，孩子从笔袋里摸出一块小橡皮。The child takes an eraser from the pencil case.

senses.title: A rubber for pencil marks
senses.definition: a small rubber for removing pencil marks
senses.definitionCN: 擦去铅笔痕迹的小块橡胶
senses.example: May I borrow your eraser?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以借你的橡皮吗？
senses.why: Eraser is erase plus -er, 'the thing that erases'; the small rubber was named for its single job of wiping out pencil marks.
senses.whyCN: eraser 是 erase 加 -er，即「擦除的东西」；这块小橡胶因专门擦掉铅笔痕而得名。

senses.title: A pad for the board
senses.definition: a larger pad for cleaning a board
senses.example: The teacher wiped the board with an eraser.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用黑板擦擦干净了黑板。
senses.why: The same tool name covers the bigger pad used on boards, because both remove the marks left by writing.
senses.whyCN: 同一类工具名也指擦黑板的大块用具，因为两者都是擦去书写留下的痕迹。

senses.title: The eraser tool
senses.definition: the eraser tool in drawing software

senses.example: Click the eraser to remove the line.
senses.exampleCN: 点橡皮工具删掉这条线。

senses.whyCN: 软件借用了实物工具的名字，把删除笔画的按钮叫作橡皮，保留了「擦掉」的画面。

definition_en: each one of a group, or at regular intervals
core_image: 老师把一摞书一本本发下去，每个孩子手上都有一本
scene: 老师把一摞书一本本发下去，每个孩子都拿到一本。Every child gets a book.
sceneCN: 这里 every 是「每一个」（第 01 个义项）；句意是每个孩子都拿到一本书。

senses.title: Each member
senses.definition: each one of a group, taken one by one
senses.example: Every child gets a book.
senses.exampleCN: 每个孩子都拿到一本书。
senses.why: Old English had æfre ælc, 'ever each'; the two words fused into one determiner that takes the members of a group one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 古英语有 æfre ælc，意为「每一个」，两个词合成一个限定词，表示把一组里的成员逐个算上。

senses.title: At fixed intervals
senses.definition: at intervals of a stated length
senses.example: The bus comes every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车每十分钟来一班。
senses.why: The 'each' idea applied to a stretch of time gives the interval sense: each ten-minute period brings one bus.
senses.whyCN: 把「每一个」用在时间段上就产生间隔义：每一个十分钟就有一班车。

senses.title: All possible
senses.definition: all the possible
senses.example: She has every reason to be proud.
senses.exampleCN: 她有充分的理由感到自豪。
senses.why: Because each single reason is counted, the word can stress that none is missing, and so it came to mean 'all possible'.
senses.whyCN: 因为连每一个理由都算上，这个词就能强调一个也不缺，于是有了「所有可能的」这一意思。

definition_en: to make someone eager, to stir up a feeling, or to make a body part active
core_image: 好消息传进教室，孩子们一下子欢呼起来
scene: 好消息传进教室，孩子们一下子欢呼起来。The good news excited the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 excite 是「使兴奋」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这个好消息让全班都兴奋起来。

senses.title: To make eager
senses.definition: to make someone feel eager and happy
senses.example: The good news excited the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 这个好消息让全班都兴奋起来。
senses.why: Latin excitare meant 'call out, stir up', from ex- 'out' and citare 'set in motion'; English keeps the image of stirring something into action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 excitare 意为「唤起、搅动」，由 ex-「向外」与 citare「使动起来」组成；英语保留的就是把某物搅动起来的画面。

senses.title: To arouse curiosity
senses.definition: to arouse interest or curiosity
senses.example: The strange box excited her curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 那个奇怪的盒子激起了她的好奇心。
senses.why: When what is stirred is curiosity, the verb names the cause of that particular feeling rather than general high spirits.
senses.whyCN: 被搅动的是好奇心时，这个词就指引起这种特定感受，而不是泛指情绪高涨。

senses.title: To cause a reaction
senses.definition: to cause a reaction or strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 引发某种反应或强烈情绪
senses.example: His joke excited laughter in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话引起满屋笑声。
senses.why: The same 'stir up' image applies to any response the subject sets off, such as laughter or anger.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「搅动」的画面也用于主语引发的任何反应，如笑声或怒气。

senses.title: To stimulate a nerve
senses.definition: to make a nerve or organ active
senses.example: The medicine excites the nerves.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药刺激神经。
senses.why: Physiology took the verb in its plainest sense: a stimulus literally stirs a nerve into activity.
senses.whyCN: 生理学取它最字面的意思：刺激物确实把神经搅动起来，使其活跃。

definition_en: physical activity for health, a practice task, or the use of a power
core_image: 清晨的公园里，老人沿着小路慢跑，呼吸平稳
scene: 清晨的公园里，老人沿着小路慢跑，呼吸平稳。The old man exercises in the park every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 exercise 是「锻炼」（第 01 个义项）；句意是每天锻炼让他身体强壮。

senses.title: Physical training
senses.definition: physical activity that keeps you healthy
senses.definitionCN: 为健康进行的身体活动
senses.example: Daily exercise keeps him strong.
senses.exampleCN: 每天锻炼让他身体强壮。
senses.why: Latin exercitium meant 'training', from exercere 'keep busy, drive on'; the body's training kept the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 exercitium 意为「训练」，来自 exercere「使忙碌、驱策」；身体的训练沿用了这个词。

senses.title: A practice task
senses.definition: a task set for practice in a book
senses.example: Do the exercises on page ten.
senses.exampleCN: 做第十页的练习题。
senses.why: The same training idea moved from the body to the mind, naming written tasks that train a skill.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「训练」的意思从身体转到头脑，用来指训练某项技能的书面题目。

senses.title: The use of a right
senses.definition: the use of a power or right
senses.example: The police exercised their right to search.
senses.exampleCN: 警方行使了搜查权。
senses.why: Exercere also meant 'put into action'; a right that is put to work in practice is said to be exercised.
senses.whyCN: exercere 也有「付诸行动」的意思；一项权利在实际中动用起来，就叫作被行使。

senses.title: To train the body
senses.definition: to take physical exercise
senses.example: She exercises every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上锻炼。
senses.why: The noun became a verb in English, as with many activity nouns, meaning to perform the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在英语里转化为动词，和许多活动类名词一样，表示进行这项活动本身。

definition_en: a public show of works or objects, or a display of a quality
core_image: 美术馆的长厅里挂满画作，人们沿着墙慢慢看
scene: 美术馆的长厅里挂满画作，人们沿着墙慢慢看。We visited the art exhibition on Sunday.
sceneCN: 这里 exhibition 是「展览会」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们星期天去看了那场美术展。

senses.title: A public show
senses.definition: a public show of works or objects
senses.definitionCN: 公开展出作品或物品的活动
senses.example: We visited the art exhibition on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们星期天去看了那场美术展。
senses.why: From Latin exhibeo 'hold out, present', through French; the noun names the organised event where things are held out to view.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 exhibeo「伸出、呈现」，经法语进入英语；这个词指把东西伸出来给人看的活动。

senses.title: The act of showing
senses.definition: the act of showing something to the public
senses.definitionCN: 把某物公开展出的行为
senses.example: The exhibition of the new car drew crowds.
senses.exampleCN: 新车的展示引来人群。
senses.why: The same noun can name the showing itself rather than the event, as when a single object is put on display.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可以指展示这个行为本身而不是整场活动，比如把单件物品摆出来给人看。

senses.title: A display of a quality
senses.definition: a display of a skill, quality or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 技能、品质或情感的显露
senses.example: His calm was a fine exhibition of courage.
senses.exampleCN: 他的镇定是勇气的出色表现。
senses.why: Because showing is the core idea, the word extends to any visible display of a quality, not only objects in a hall.
senses.whyCN: 因为「展示」是核心意思，这个词也扩展到任何看得见的品质流露，而不只是展厅里的物件。
